from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Putnam problems prioritize elegance over brute force.", "Standard math uses hammers for nuts.", "Putnam math analyzes structural stress points."]
        self.setup_layout("The Putnam Mindset: Beyond Standard Algorithms", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        title_highlight = Text("Beyond Standard", font_size=28, color="#FFD700")
        problem_symbol = RegularPolygon(n=5, color="#00CED1")
        solution_symbol = Star(n=5, color="#FF4500")
        summary_text = Text("Elegance wins.", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Putnam problems prioritize elegance over brute force.
        self.play(FadeIn(self.title))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(problem_symbol, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(problem_symbol))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Standard math uses hammers for nuts.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00CED1")
        # Visual transition
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Putnam math analyzes structural stress points.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.play(Transform(problem_symbol, solution_symbol))
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(problem_symbol), FadeOut(self.lecture), FadeOut(self.title))
        self.place_in_area(summary_text, 'C2', 'D5')
        self.play(FadeIn(summary_text))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Existence proofs often rely on extremes.",
            "Pigeonhole Principle forces structural overlap.",
            "Extremal thinking simplifies complex constraints."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Tactical Tool: The Pigeonhole Principle & Extremal Thinking", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show title: Pigeonhole & Extremal (#FFD700) fade in.
        title_highlight = Text("Pigeonhole & Extremal", font_size=32, color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(title_highlight, 'A3')
        self.play(FadeIn(title_highlight))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate objects filling pigeonholes (#00CED1).
        holes = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.6, color="#00CED1") for _ in range(4)])
        holes.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(holes, 'C2')
        
        pigeons = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.2, color="#FFFFFF", fill_opacity=1) for _ in range(5)])
        
        self.play(FadeIn(holes))
        for p in pigeons:
            self.play(FadeIn(p.move_to(holes[0].get_center())), run_time=0.3)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00CED1"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight maximum/minimum elements in #FF4500.
        extremes = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#FF4500") for _ in range(5)])
        self.place_at_grid(extremes, 'E3')
        
        # Highlight the largest dot
        max_dot = extremes[4].copy().set_color("#FF4500").scale(1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(extremes), FadeIn(max_dot))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Integration: Bridging Calculus and Combinatorics", [
            "Integrate disparate fields for stronger solutions.", 
            "Riemann Sums bound discrete counting problems.", 
            "Geometric integrals model complex combinatorial structures."
        ])
        
        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show title: Calculus & Combinatorics
        title_art = Tex(r"Calculus \& Combinatorics", color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(title_art, "B3", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(title_art))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display integral symbol morphing into sum
        integral = MathTex(r"\int", color="#00CED1")
        summation = MathTex(r"\sum", color="#00CED1")
        self.place_at_grid(integral, "E2", scale_factor=3.0)
        self.play(Write(integral))
        self.play(Transform(integral, summation))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00CED1")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Combine curves and discrete points
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 3], y_range=[0, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: x**2/3, color="#FF4500")
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(axes.c2p(i, (i**2)/3), color="#FF4500") for i in [0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5]])
        combined = VGroup(axes, curve, dots)
        self.place_in_area(combined, "A4", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(combined))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis: The Final Countdown", [
            "Identify the invariant.",
            "Test the extreme case.",
            "Connect abstractions to original constraints."
        ])

        # Animation Elements
        clock_gear_base = Circle(radius=1.2, color="#FFD700", stroke_width=4)
        gear_teeth = VGroup(*[Line(UP*1.2, UP*1.4, color="#FFD700") for _ in range(12)]).arrange_submobjects(ORIGIN)
        for i, tooth in enumerate(gear_teeth):
            tooth.rotate(i * PI/6, about_point=ORIGIN)
        
        clock_gear = VGroup(clock_gear_base, gear_teeth)
        self.place_at_grid(clock_gear, 'C3', scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.title), run_time=1)
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"), FadeIn(clock_gear))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00CED1"))
        self.play(Rotate(clock_gear, angle=2*PI, run_time=2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00CED1"))
        flash = Flash(self.grid['C3'], color="#FFFFFF", line_length=0.5, num_lines=16)
        self.play(flash, run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Mastering the Putnam: The Art of Creative Problem-Solving

sections.title: The Putnam Mindset: Beyond Standard Algorithms
sections.content: Introduction to the Putnam philosophy: Problems aren't about brute force, but 'mathematical elegance.' We define the transition from high-school procedural math to competition-level logical synthesis.
sections.example: Visualize a squirrel trying to crack a nut: Standard math uses a hammer; Putnam math analyzes the nut's structural stress points to find the single hairline fracture.

sections.title: Core Strategy: Invariant Analysis
sections.content: Introduce 'Invariants'—quantities or properties that remain unchanged under a system's transformation. Prerequisite: Basic modular arithmetic and parity concepts. Graphical representation: A flow chart showing a dynamic state machine where one specific value remains constant.
sections.example: A room full of chameleons changing colors. By tracking the parity of color counts (the invariant), we prove whether they can ever all become the same color.

sections.title: Tactical Tool: The Pigeonhole Principle & Extremal Thinking
sections.content: How to handle existence proofs. We focus on the 'Extremal Principle'—examining the smallest or largest configuration to force a contradiction or discovery.
sections.example: A robotic arm placing sensors on a grid. We use the 'Pigeonhole Principle' to show that if you have N+1 sensors and N spots, at least one spot must have two sensors, triggering a logic circuit.

sections.title: Integration: Bridging Calculus and Combinatorics
sections.content: Putnam problems often bridge disparate fields. We demonstrate how to apply Integral Bounds to solve discrete counting problems, visualised as area under a curve representing discrete bars.
sections.example: Using the 'Riemann Sum' approximation to bound the number of paths a robot can take through a maze, turning a complex summation into a smooth geometric integral.

sections.title: Synthesis: The Final Countdown
sections.content: Summary of the 3-step workflow: 1. Identify the invariant, 2. Test the extreme case, 3. Connect the abstract result back to the original constraint. Encouragement to seek beauty in the proof.
sections.example: The 'Archimedes' moment: A final animation showing all disconnected strategy pieces clicking together like a complex clockwork mechanism to solve a classic 1990s Putnam challenge.
